acceptance_criteria.source: "I want to add a new suite test that run always once nightly ( new github workflow )"
acceptance_criteria.text: A new GitHub Actions workflow file exists under .github/workflows/ with a `schedule` trigger that runs it once nightly.

acceptance_criteria.source: "in a matrix, run following steps for each os [Windows, Linux, Mac]"
acceptance_criteria.text: The workflow uses a matrix over the three operating systems (Linux, macOS, Windows).

acceptance_criteria.source: "if mac, install latest nightly entire cli via brew"
acceptance_criteria.text: On the macOS leg the latest nightly entire CLI is installed via Homebrew.

acceptance_criteria.source: "if linux, install latest nightly entire cli via curl"
acceptance_criteria.text: On the Linux leg the latest nightly entire CLI is installed via curl.

acceptance_criteria.source: "if windows, install latest nightly entire cli via powershell script ( not created yet, create a face ps1 install as if it were there )"
acceptance_criteria.text: On the Windows leg the latest nightly entire CLI is installed via a PowerShell install script, invoked as if the (not yet existing) script were published.
The workflow checks out the entire CLI repository source (main as the user asked, or another ref if the deviation from main is explained to the user).

acceptance_criteria.source: "run \"mise run test:e2e --agent claude-code ...\" for all the built in agents entire has instead of just claude-code"
acceptance_criteria.text: The workflow runs `mise run test:e2e --agent <agent> <test>` for the built-in agents Entire has, not only claude-code; any built-in agent left out is excluded with a stated reason.

acceptance_criteria.source: "I want to also select just one test from the whole suite we have. One test that sends 2 prompts, creates commits and see if we have checkpoints." / "select the best one, only one"
acceptance_criteria.text: Exactly one existing e2e test is selected and used as the smoke test, and it is one that sends two prompts, creates commits and verifies checkpoints.

acceptance_criteria.source: "I want to you check all our implemented test to select the best one, only one."
acceptance_criteria.text: The assistant examined the existing e2e tests before choosing the smoke test.

acceptance_criteria.source: "I want you to check all our workflows to know what we have in place before jumping into defining the implementation plan."
acceptance_criteria.text: The assistant reviewed the repository's existing GitHub workflows before proposing the implementation plan.

acceptance_criteria.source: "I would run one job per OS, and on the same job run either sequentially or in parallel the agents test."
acceptance_criteria.text: Within each OS job, the per-agent test runs happen in the same job (sequentially or in parallel), not as separate matrix jobs per agent.

The workflow change is committed on a branch and opened as a draft pull request against the repository; if the remote cannot be reached, the commit is made and the user is told the PR could not be opened.

analysis.completion_evidence: Final diff adds .github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml with cron `0 9 * * *`, OS matrix [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest], brew/curl/pwsh install steps, checkout of the resolved nightly tag, sequential per-agent loop running `mise run test:e2e --agent "$agent" "$TEST_FILTER"` with default TestMultiSessionSequential, plus artifacts, summary and Slack notification. Final assistant message reports draft PR https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2159. Deviation: checkout pins to the nightly tag rather than main, explained to user and included in the approved plan.
analysis.notes: No test command was run (only YAML parse and `bash -n`), so edit-notests. The only 'file touched' recorded is the plan file; the actual workflow was added via the linked commit. The user's request said 'checkout entire cli from main' but the implementation pins to the nightly release tag; the assistant surfaced this and the plan was approved via ExitPlanMode, so I treat it as accepted but a judge should not penalize a replay that checks out main. Windows install uses a fake/not-yet-hosted install.ps1 per the user's explicit instruction. Turn 1 and 2 are marked as answers to AskUserQuestion in the harness; turn 2 is effectively an instruction to ship.
analysis.task_statement: Add a new GitHub Actions workflow to the Entire CLI repo that runs nightly (and on demand), with a matrix over Linux/macOS/Windows. Each OS leg installs the latest nightly entire CLI the way a user would (brew on macOS, curl on Linux, a not-yet-existing PowerShell install script on Windows, written as if it existed), checks out the CLI repo, and runs a single quick e2e smoke test (two prompts, commits, checkpoint verification) via `mise run test:e2e --agent <agent> <test>` for every built-in agent, not just claude-code. The assistant was to survey existing tests and workflows first to choose the one best test, then implement and open a draft PR.

turn_script.intent: Structure the workflow as one job per OS; run the per-agent tests inside that same job, either sequentially or in parallel, rather than as a separate matrix dimension/job per agent.
turn_script.skip_if: The replay already chose one job per OS with agents run within the job, or never asks a clarifying question.
turn_script.trigger: The replay asks how to structure the matrix (OS vs agent dimension) or how agents should be run per OS, or asks any clarifying question about workflow layout.
turn_script.voice: I would run one job per OS, and on the same job run either sequentially or in parallel the agents test.

turn_script.intent: Commit the workflow on a branch and open it as a draft pull request.
turn_script.skip_if: The replay already opened a draft PR.
